findings.title: Realizable-solvency value leak: surplus / solvency / totalBalanceOf priced at the VAULT rate but value is only realizable at the AMM rate; skim strips the discount buffer, socializing a principal shortfall onto last-out stakers
findings.severityEscalation: approaches High during an sUSDe AMM discount event (proportional to the live AMM/vault gap; sUSDe has historically discounted several percent in stress)

sources.note: YIELD-PRINCIPAL-ACCOUNTING-SKEW: skim drains the deposit-time haircut buffer that would cushion the exit -- same mechanism
vault-rate vs AMM-realizable divergence handed to econ-scanner

findings.rootCause: Every economically-critical quantity (minOut, totalBalanceOf, per-client surplus, the skim aggregate-surplus ceiling, and the 'provable solvency invariant') is denominated at vault.convertToAssets/convertToShares (the vault rate), but the restricted shares can only be realized at the Curve AMM rate. skimSurplus harvests the vault-rate surplus (which includes the deposit-time slippage-haircut buffer), so after a skim the shares remaining to back principal are worth less than principal at the only realizable rate; under an AMM discount the last-out staker eats a socialized shortfall.
findings.empiricalProof: Tier-3 STILL-FAILING invariant: both forge invariant_realizableSolvency and medusa property_realizableSolvency break with the minimal sequence deposit -> skim -> AMM-discount (forge counterexample: realizable 0.912e18 < principal 0.950e18; medusa: held 626988.6e18 * q 0.9717e18 < principal). Deterministic PoCs logged a 28.5e18 shortfall and a 48.5e18 last-out swing.
findings.consolidationRationale: ECON-001 is the flagship interaction finding; the realizableSolvency invariant failure (forge+medusa) is its empirical counterexample and is carried here as first-class evidence; PATTERN-003 and profile scannerAttention#1 are the Tier-1 precursors of the same vault-rate-vs-AMM-rate root cause.

findings.title: Uncapped withdraw over-delivery: full AMM output forwarded to recipient while principal debited only by requested amount; surplus leaks outside skimSurplus (surplus-routing invariant breach)

sources.evidence: test_ECON002_ordinary_withdraw_extracts_skimmable_surplus PASS: ordinary withdraw pocketed 100e18 of skimmable surplus

sources.note: uncapped withdraw upside, deferred to econ/interaction
spec-conformance angle: 'all rounding favors the protocol' is one-directional in code (story-038/043)

REFUTATION COMPANION: surplus S*p-D is invariant under withdrawal, so this is NOT cross-client theft -- it is surplus MIS-ROUTING (paid to withdrawer instead of skim recipient); also flags the inaccurate 'accumulates as protocol-owned yield' docstring for the AMM-slippage component
supports CODE-006: other clients' backing untouched; confirms severity is surplus-misallocation, not external theft

findings.rootCause: minOut floors the downside but nothing caps the upside: when the AMM realizable rate r=P_amm/P_vault > 1, underlyingReceived = amount*r is forwarded in full to the recipient while only `amount` of principal is burned, so the excess amount*(r-1) -- exactly the value skimSurplus is meant to route to the protocol -- is captured by whichever path (withdraw vs skim) runs first.
findings.consolidationRationale: Single code path (line 367 vs 371) seen by four scanners from four angles: ECON-002 (economic), LOCAL-MKT-002 (Tier-1 local-high), FAITH-001 (spec-conformance), CODE-006 (interaction refutation). CODE-006 is retained as the refutation companion because it correctly narrows the impact (surplus mis-routing, not cross-client theft) -- load-bearing for honest severity. surplus_routing invariant breach is the empirical proof.
findings.severityNuance: Tempered toward Medium/Low because the extra value is paid by the AMM counterparty (not other clients) and all authorized clients are protocol-owned -- a defeat of skim's surplus-routing role rather than external theft. Final call to severity-classifier.

findings.title: emergencyWithdraw accounting desync: raw vault shares moved to owner without decrementing clientBalances/totalDeposited and without pausing -> principal ledger overstates backing, first-come-first-served drain of remaining clients (owner footgun)

sources.note: observationsNotFindings: no story pins a principal update on emergency, so not a Law-2 violation -- routed to operational-hazard lane
econ-scanner deferred to this finding to avoid duplication

findings.rootCause: emergencyWithdraw (onlyOwner, NOT nonReentrant, NOT whenNotPaused) transfers min(amount, heldShares) of raw vault shares to owner() while leaving clientBalances/totalDeposited intact and the contract live. A partial emergency withdrawal on a live contract leaves principalOf/getTotalDeposited overstating recoverable backing; later withdraw()/withdrawAsOwner() cap sharesToSell to the reduced pool but still debit full requested principal, making early withdrawers whole at the expense of later ones.
findings.consolidationRationale: Tier-1 (LOCAL-MKT-003), Tier-2 code-scanner (CODE-001), faithfulness observation, and econ-scanner suppressed-note all point at lines 386-395; consolidated as a single owner footgun (Law-3 operational hazard, non-obvious consequence).
findings.safeConfigGuidance: Treat emergencyWithdraw as terminal/migration: pause() first, or proportionally reduce clientBalances/totalDeposited (or pull the FULL share balance only).

findings.title: slippageToleranceBps overloaded as principal-credit haircut with no sane upper bound: a well-intentioned tolerance increase silently under-credits every depositor's principal; at MAX_BPS it credits zero principal AND sets minOut=0 (owner footgun)

sources.note: CENTRALIZATION-ADMIN: same overloaded parameter, MAX_BPS zeroes principal credit + slippage floor

findings.rootCause: slippageToleranceBps is a single owner parameter controlling BOTH the AMM swap floor minOut AND credited principal via _creditedPrincipal(amount)=amount*(MAX_BPS-bps)/MAX_BPS, booked into clientBalances/totalDeposited. setSlippageTolerance validates only _bps<=MAX_BPS; there is no lower sanity ceiling, so raising tolerance to absorb a wider AMM spread silently haircuts every subsequent deposit's recoverable principal by the same proportion. At bps=MAX_BPS, creditedPrincipal==0 and minOut==0 (deposit swaps full input but books zero principal, and slippage protection is disabled).
findings.consolidationRationale: CODE-002 (Tier-2) and PATTERN-004 (Tier-1 pattern-db) are the same overloaded-parameter footgun; merged. Note: the MAX_BPS==minOut-collapse extreme is an OBVIOUS misconfig (econ-scanner correctly suppressed that sub-case under Law 3); the IN-SCOPE footgun is the NON-OBVIOUS principal-haircut coupling at moderate, plausible tolerance values (e.g. 2000 bps).
findings.safeConfigGuidance: Decouple the swap slippage floor from the principal-credit haircut, OR add a conservative upper bound to setSlippageTolerance and document that the parameter haircuts credited principal.

findings.title: MEV sandwich + missing swap deadline: every value-moving swap derives its slippage floor from the same-tx vault spot rate via a single owner param, with no per-call minOut and no deadline on the Curve path

sources.note: MISSING-SLIPPAGE: no deadline, caller cannot supply minOut, minOut can be 0 for dust / at MAX_BPS
reentrancy-events on swap confirms the adapter performs an unguarded external call to Curve Router NG (supporting context for the swap path)

findings.rootCause: minOut = (vault-rate value)*(1-slip) is anchored to the slowly-moving vault rate, not the execution venue, and ICurveRouterNG.exchange carries no deadline (confirmed: no deadline parameter exists in the interface). A searcher can front-run the strategy's Curve swap to the slip boundary (fill still >= minOut, no revert) and back-run, extracting up to slip*tradeSize; a builder can hold a deadline-less tx for the worst in-band block. The actual value owner (staker/client) cannot pass a tighter minOut or deadline -- the only knob is one global owner param.
findings.consolidationRationale: ECON-003 (Tier-2) and PATTERN-002 (Tier-1) describe the same MEV/missing-deadline/spot-anchored-floor root cause; merged. STATIC-014 (reentrancy-events on swap) is supporting context only. Magnitude is Medium (bounded by slippageToleranceBps and compressed by the deep live sUSDe/USDe Curve pool).
findings.recommendation: Add a deadline to the swap path; allow callers to pass an explicit minOut (max(callerMinOut, ownerFloor)); consider a manipulation-resistant quote instead of same-tx spot.

findings.title: slippageToleranceBps default 0 deposit/withdraw DoS: default demands full vault-rate execution (strictest floor), so every deposit/withdraw reverts on minOut from construction until owner sets a non-zero tolerance (owner footgun, fails-closed)
findings.rootCause: At slippageToleranceBps=0 (the constructed default), deposit minOut=convertToShares(amount) and withdraw minOut=idealUnderlying demand the FULL vault-rate fair value -- which a real Curve swap (spread + curve) essentially never returns -- so all flows revert until setSlippageTolerance(bps>0). The inverted semantics (0 reads as 'lenient' but encodes the strictest possible floor) is the non-obvious part.
findings.consolidationRationale: CODE-003 and LOCAL-MKT-001 are the same default-config DoS. Kept SEPARATE from DEDUP-004 despite sharing the slippageToleranceBps parameter: different failure mode (fails-closed availability DoS at bps=0 vs silent principal-haircut value loss at high bps) and different mitigation (require non-zero at construction vs cap upper bound).
findings.impact: Availability only -- fails closed, no fund loss.

findings.title: convert* used as in-tx slippage oracle: donation/flash-manipulable for a GENERIC ERC4626 vault (safe for the wired sUSDe deployment) -- deployment-conditional design constraint
findings.conditionalSeverity: High if ever wired to a small/new/manipulable ERC4626 vault (full slippage-protection bypass)

sources.note: implausible for sUSDe (live); plausible only for a future thin-vault deployment
FLASH-LOAN-PRICE: flagged High on impact, confidence about applicability; SCOPED DOWN by ECON-004 after sUSDe-specific analysis

findings.rootCause: Every slippage floor is derived from vault.convertToShares/convertToAssets read in the same tx as the swap. The strategy is immutable-generic over any IERC4626 vault. For a small/freshly-seeded vault, convertToAssets is donation/flash-manipulable (classic ERC4626 inflation), letting an attacker collapse minOut ahead of the Curve swap and sandwich it. sUSDe (multi-billion TVL, ~8h reward vesting) is NOT manipulable, so the live deployment is safe.
findings.consolidationRationale: PATTERN-001 (Tier-1, potential-high) and ECON-004 (Tier-2, scoped-low after sUSDe analysis) are the same spot-convert*-as-oracle root cause; merged. Reported as a scoped DESIGN CONSTRAINT with a demonstrated root cause in current code, NOT a speculative future-code exploit. FLAGGED FOR HUMAN REVIEW because the Tier-1 High framing vs Tier-2 low (deployment-conditional) framing is a severity divergence the classifier should adjudicate.
findings.recommendation: Document/enforce that this strategy may only be wired to ERC4626 vaults whose convertToAssets is not single-block manipulable (deep TVL + reward vesting).

findings.title: CurveAMMAdapter.setRoute endpoint-only validation: swapParams coin indices, pools array, and reverse-route inverse-consistency are not validated on-chain (owner footgun; Slither lastToken flag is a false positive)

sources.disposition: FALSE POSITIVE -- Slither uninitialized-local on `lastToken` (L74): the loop always runs and path[0]==tokenIn is required non-zero, so lastToken is always assigned before the require. Dismissed by CODE-004.

findings.rootCause: setRoute validates only path endpoints (path[0]==tokenIn, last-non-zero==tokenOut). swapParams ([i,j,swap_type,pool_type,n_coins]), the pools array, and whether routes[tokenOut][tokenIn] is the true mathematical inverse are NOT validated on-chain; swap()/isPairFullyConfigured() check only the reverse direction's .configured FLAG. A wrong coin index/pool or non-inverse reverse route passes validation.
findings.consolidationRationale: CODE-004 and LOCAL-CRV-001 are the same endpoint-only-validation footgun; STATIC-008's lastToken flag is the false positive that CODE-004 explicitly dismisses -- folded here so the false positive is recorded with its refutation. Blast radius is bounded: Curve Router NG reverts on a genuinely invalid route and minOut floors every swap, so a bad route causes a reverting/DoS'd swap, NOT silent value mis-delivery (no on-chain theft under the trusted-router assumption).
findings.safeConfigGuidance: Treat AMMRoutes.json correctness and reverse-inverse consistency as a deploy-time review gate; document on-chain validation is endpoint-only.

findings.title: Checks-Effects-Interactions violation in deposit/withdraw (state written after external swap/transfer): REFUTED as exploitable under the non-hooked-ERC20 trust model; retained as a documented latent assumption
findings.disposition: REFUTED as exploitable; latent if a transfer-hook/FoT/ERC777 token is ever wired in

sources.verdict: REFUTED as exploitable -- nonReentrant + non-hooked ERC20 fully neutralize

sources.note: reentrancy-no-eth _withdrawInternal
reentrancy-no-eth _totalWithdraw
reentrancy-benign _withdrawInternal
reentrancy-benign _depositInternal
reentrancy-events swap (also cross-listed as supporting context in DEDUP-005)

findings.rootCause: Both _depositInternal (state at 322-323 after the swap) and _withdrawInternal (state at 371-372 after the swap AND the safeTransfer at 367) update clientBalances/totalDeposited after external calls -- a CEI violation. All state-mutating entry points share OZ's single-_status nonReentrant guard (cross-function re-entry blocked), and the only external calls in the stale-state window are to the trusted CurveAMMAdapter/Curve Router NG and to plain ERC20 transfer/transferFrom of the underlying + vault share token -- none yield control to attacker code under the registry trust assumptions (no transfer hooks / FoT / ERC777). With no attacker callback, read-only reentrancy against the unguarded views (totalBalanceOf/principalOf) is unreachable.
findings.consolidationRationale: Six Slither reentrancy/CEI flags (STATIC-006/007/012/013/014), the Tier-1 LOCAL-MKT-005, and the Tier-2 CODE-007 all describe the same effects-after-interactions pattern. Consolidated into one informational finding. Per Law 1 recall, NOT dropped: retained as a documented latent assumption that becomes live only if a hooked/FoT token is ever wired in (explicitly out of the current trust model). See also parked PATTERN-ML-002 (read-only-reentrancy lens) in manual-review.json.

findings.title: _totalWithdraw state-inconsistency: migration recorded as executed even when sharesToSell floors to 0 (tiny-balance client), and Phase-1 cached `amount` is decorative (live clientBalances used). Slither incorrect-equality at L410 is benign.

sources.disposition: BENIGN -- Slither incorrect-equality at L410 (totalShares==0 || totalDeposited==0) is a correct literal-0 compare; dismissed by CODE-005.

sources.note: observationsNotFindings: Phase-2 ignores cached snapshot, re-reads live clientBalances; no story-036 criterion pins to snapshot -> documented quirk

findings.rootCause: _executeWithdrawal resets the two-phase WithdrawalState and emits WithdrawalExecuted BEFORE calling _totalWithdraw (correct CEI), but _totalWithdraw only zeroes clientBalances and decrements totalDeposited INSIDE `if (sharesToSell > 0)`. For a client whose live balance is a tiny fraction of totalDeposited, sharesToSell can floor to 0; the function returns having moved nothing and left principal on the books, yet the state machine is reset and the migration recorded as executed. Separately, _totalWithdraw reads clientBalances live and ignores the Phase-1 cached `amount` (used only for the >0 guard), so a balance change between the 24h phases is silently honored.
findings.consolidationRationale: CODE-005 (Tier-2), STATIC-005 (the benign incorrect-equality it dismisses), and the faithfulness cached-vs-live observation all sit on lines 404-435; merged. Direction is benign (no fund loss -- the un-migrated client retains full principal); the hazard is operational (owner may believe a migration completed when it did not).
findings.impact: Operational/state-handling only; no fund loss. QA-level.

findings.title: 'Provable solvency invariant' overstated: ERC4626 double round-down means convertToAssets(convertToShares(creditedPrincipal)) can be a few wei below creditedPrincipal, so fairValue >= creditedPrincipal is provable only up to rounding dust

sources.note: story-043 'provable solvency invariant' claim overstatement

findings.rootCause: minOut=convertToShares(creditedPrincipal) guarantees sharesReceived>=minOut, but because convertToShares and convertToAssets both round DOWN, convertToAssets(convertToShares(creditedPrincipal)) can be < creditedPrincipal by sub-wei/few-wei dust, so the chain proves fairValue >= (a value possibly below creditedPrincipal), not >= creditedPrincipal. Accumulates on flat markets.
findings.consolidationRationale: FAITH-002 (spec-conformance) and LOCAL-MKT-004 (Tier-1) are the same rounding-dust observation; merged. Conservative crediting intent is faithfully implemented -- only the absoluteness of the 'provable' qualifier is overstated. QA/documentation-level.
findings.recommendation: Acknowledge the dust in the invariant claim (fairValue >= creditedPrincipal - dust) or add a small protocol-favoring epsilon to minOut.

findings.title: skim-path loops over the authorized-client set: per-iteration external vault.convertToShares call + require-revert-in-loop -> owner-bounded gas-griefing/DoS if owner authorizes a very large client set

sources.note: calls-loop: vault.convertToShares(surplus) inside the client loop
require-revert-in-loop _accrueSurplusShares (client != address(0))
require-revert-in-loop _distributeBuffer

findings.rootCause: _accrueSurplusShares and _distributeBuffer iterate over the full _authorizedClients set within a single skimSurplus call, making a per-iteration external vault.convertToShares call and a require inside the loop. A single bad client entry reverts the whole batch, and a very large set could exceed the block gas limit and make skimSurplus uncallable.
findings.consolidationRationale: Three Slither flags (STATIC-011 calls-loop, STATIC-023/024 require-revert-in-loop) on the same skim-path loop; merged. The client set is owner-curated (setClient) and expected small (protocol contracts), so this is owner-bounded, not attacker-extendable -- a mild Law-3 footgun. See also parked PATTERN-ML-003 (DOS-UNBOUNDED-LOOP) in manual-review.json.
findings.impact: Owner-bounded availability of skimSurplus; low priority.

findings.title: nonReentrant is not the first modifier on 6 functions (defense-in-depth note): every preceding modifier is a no-external-call auth/access check, so the guard always engages before any external interaction
findings.function: totalWithdrawal, skimSurplus, deposit, withdraw, depositAsOwner, withdrawAsOwner
findings.rootCause: Aderyn non-reentrant-not-first across 6 functions. In every case the preceding modifier is an auth/access check (onlyOwner / onlyAuthorizedClient / onlyAuthorizedWithdrawer) that performs NO external call, so the reentrancy guard is effectively engaged before any interaction.
findings.consolidationRationale: Six identical Aderyn flags consolidated into one defense-in-depth note (instance count preserved). Genuinely low/QA -- no preceding modifier makes an external call, so there is no live reentrancy window. Retained at informational per Law-1 recall rather than dropped, but flagged as ordering-style only.

findings.title: block.timestamp drives the two-phase withdrawal window (24h waiting / 48h execution): timestamp-dependence is load-bearing and intended; confirm window bounds cannot be straddled by miner drift

sources.note: KEPT per audit policy: time-driven protocol, timestamp logic is load-bearing

findings.rootCause: _updateWithdrawalStatus uses block.timestamp for the two-phase window comparisons (>= initiatedAt+WAITING_PERIOD, <= initiatedAt+TOTAL_DURATION, > initiatedAt+TOTAL_DURATION). The 24h/48h windows are far larger than any plausible miner timestamp drift (~12s), so straddling is not exploitable, but kept visible per policy for a time-driven protocol.
findings.consolidationRationale: Single Slither timestamp flag, kept per the static stage's explicit Law-1 policy note (not noise-filtered). Negligible drift impact on a 24h/48h window -> informational.

findings.title: Unit-mismatch footgun: setAsideBufferSize is a PERCENT (0-100) while slippageToleranceBps is BPS (0-10000) -- mixing the two mental models is an owner footgun
findings.rootCause: Two owner-set parameters use different unit conventions (percent 0-100 vs bps 0-10000). An owner passing 50 expecting 0.5% (or vice versa) would misconfigure. Both are owner-gated and documented, but the inconsistency is a latent footgun.
findings.consolidationRationale: Single Tier-1 base-profile observation; QA-level owner-config hygiene note.
findings.recommendation: Standardize on one unit convention or clearly document the difference at each setter.

findings.title: totalWithdrawal carries whenNotPaused: a Global-Pauser pause blocks the two-phase emergency migration path until unpause (degraded availability; emergencyWithdraw remains)
findings.rootCause: totalWithdrawal is whenNotPaused, so a pause blocks even legitimate migration until unpause. emergencyWithdraw (no pause gate) remains available to the owner, so this is a degraded-availability note, not a lockup.
findings.consolidationRationale: Single Tier-1 base-profile observation; QA-level availability note.
findings.impact: Degraded availability only; emergencyWithdraw is the unblocked owner fallback.

findings.title: CurveAMMAdapter has no rescue/sweep function: tokens accidentally sent, or dust left if the router ever under-consumes amountIn, are permanently stranded
findings.rootCause: No onlyOwner sweep/rescue. Router output goes to msg.sender (not the adapter), so the adapter retains nothing in the happy path; this is only an edge/operator concern for accidentally-sent tokens or under-consume dust.
findings.consolidationRationale: Single Tier-1 adapter-profile observation; QA-level, negligible given the stateless design.
findings.recommendation: Consider an onlyOwner rescue for stranded tokens, or accept as negligible.

findings.title: setClient ignores the bool return of EnumerableSet.add/remove: idempotent re-adds / removal of a non-member silently succeed (caller cannot distinguish a no-op from an effective change)

sources.note: slither:unused-return / aderyn:unchecked-return on EnumerableSet.add
slither:unused-return / aderyn:unchecked-return on EnumerableSet.remove

findings.rootCause: setClient ignores the bool return of EnumerableSet.add/remove, so an idempotent re-add or a removal of a non-member silently emits success; the caller cannot distinguish a no-op from an effective change.
findings.consolidationRationale: Two corroborated Slither+Aderyn unused-return flags on the same setter; merged. Benign (set membership is still correct) -- QA at best.

sources.note: conformant (code) with a doc-staleness note; surfaced for qa-bundler

findings.title: Integration caveat: skimSurplus return value (post-swap underlying delivered) can differ substantially from the sum of SurplusSkimmed.amount events (pre-swap vault-asset snapshot) -- downstream must not assume equality

sources.note: documented in IYieldStrategy semantics
ensure downstream bookkeeping does not assume equality

findings.rootCause: skimSurplus returns the post-swap underlying actually delivered, while SurplusSkimmed events carry the pre-swap snapshot in vault-asset terms; these can diverge by the AMM execution gap. A downstream consumer (e.g. stableYieldAccumulator) that assumes equality would mis-account.
findings.consolidationRationale: Interface criticalSemantics + profile scannerAttention#4 describe the same documented divergence; merged as an integration caveat. It IS documented in NatSpec, so QA/informational -- surfaced so the divergence is not silently relied upon downstream.
findings.impact: Integration accounting hazard for downstream consumers; documented design behavior.

No collision-sensitive sink. Aderyn High dismissed; recorded here visibly per Law-1 rather than silently dropped.
